faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on my UQ salary?

Our calculator estimates super at 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Hourly Rate and Annual Salary

Whether you are negotiating a new role at The University of Queensland or checking your current pay, converting an hourly rate to an annual salary is a key step. This guide explains the calculation, the role of the National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading, and how tax and super affect your take-home pay. We use the keyword **uq salary** throughout to help you relate these concepts to a real enterprise agreement.

### The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the Fair Work Commission set the national minimum wage at $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week, or $1,004.90 per week. This is the base rate for adult employees not covered by an award or agreement. Most employees, including those at UQ, are covered by a modern award or an enterprise agreement that sets higher minimum rates. The UQ Enterprise Agreement 2021–2026 is a closed agreement that displaces awards, but it guarantees that no base rate falls below the relevant award or minimum wage order.

### Casual Loading and the UQ Salary Example

Casual employees receive a loading instead of paid leave. Under the national minimum wage order, the casual loading is 25% on top of the base rate, making the minimum casual rate $33.05 per hour. The UQ Enterprise Agreement also provides a 25% loading for casual professional employees, in lieu of agreement-based benefits. When you use our [timesheet](/) tool, you can check a box to add 25% casual loading to your base hourly rate. Never enter a rate that already includes loading.

For a casual UQ employee on the national minimum wage, the hourly rate with loading is $33.05. If you work 38 hours per week, your annual gross pay would be $33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,306.80. This is the figure before tax and super.

### From Hourly to Annual: The Calculation

The standard formula is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

We assume 38 ordinary hours per week, which is the standard full-time week under the National Employment Standards. If you work fewer hours, adjust accordingly. The result is a gross annual figure—it does not include unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. For a more precise estimate, use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool.

For example, a UQ professional employee on a base hourly rate of $40.00 (non-casual) would have an annual gross of $40.00 × 38 × 52 = $79,040. A casual employee on the same base rate with 25% loading would have an hourly rate of $50.00 and annual gross of $98,800.

### Tax and Medicare on Your Annual Figure

Once you have your annual gross salary, you can estimate your tax and Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% of excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30% of excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37% of excess over $135,000
- $190,001 and above: $51,370 plus 45% of excess over $190,000

The Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. For low-income earners, reductions may apply. Our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this guide. The estimate does not include the Medicare levy surcharge, HELP repayments, or salary packaging.

For a UQ salary of $79,040 (non-casual), the estimated tax would be approximately $4,020 + 30% × ($79,040 – $45,000) = $4,020 + $10,212 = $14,232. Medicare levy at 2% = $1,580.80. Total deductions = $15,812.80, leaving an annual after-tax amount of about $63,227.20.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings, not deducted from your salary. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of ordinary earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. Under the UQ Enterprise Agreement, continuing and fixed-term employees receive a 17% employer contribution. Casual employees receive the minimum super guarantee rate. Our calculator estimates super at 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top. For a $79,040 salary, that would be an additional $9,484.80 per year contributed to your super fund.

### Using the Timesheet Tool

Our [timesheet](/) tool lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. It calculates your annual gross, fortnightly pay, estimated tax, Medicare, and super. You can also compare your rate to the national minimum wage and average earnings. The Australian Bureau of Statistics reported that full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 in May 2026, or about $108,352 annually. This is a useful benchmark for UQ salary negotiations.

Remember: this is an estimate. Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more details, see our [pay guides](/blog), [reference tables](/data), and [about the timesheet](/about) page.
